title: Two times for one height
caption: Height h = 20t − 5t² of a ball thrown up at 20 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). Setting h = 15 m gives a quadratic with two roots: t = 1 s on the way up and t = 3 s on the way down. The graph shows why: the line h = 15 m cuts the parabola twice, either side of the top at t = 2 s (20 m).
alt: Parabola of height against time for a ball thrown up at 20 metres per second, peaking at 20 metres at 2 seconds, with a horizontal line at 15 metres crossing it at 1 and 3 seconds.
description: Height h in metres against time t in seconds, from 0 to 4 s: h = 20t − 5t².
The curve rises to 20 m at t = 2 s and returns to the ground at t = 4 s.
The dashed line at h = 15 m meets the curve at t = 1 s (going up) and t = 3 s (coming down): the two roots of t² − 4t + 3 = 0.
